extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, trademark practitioners, registrants, and other trademark stakeholders (policymakers, attorneys, and USPTO staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Annual advisory-committee report reviewing Trademark Operations performance, metrics, initiatives, rules, and policy issues for FY2019; intended to evaluate Office performance and guide stakeholder expectations. Contains performance targets, quality measures, rule changes, IT/modernization priorities, TTAB updates, and international cooperation projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced Disposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Balanced Disposal occurs when either (1) a First Office Action issues; (2) the application is approved for publication; or (3) the application is abandoned prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019 completed 1,387,610 Balanced Disposals (exceeded planned 1,334,700). Used as a throughput metric to measure intermediate processing steps in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Office Disposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Office Disposals refers to the number of applications that resulted in either registration or abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There were 609,124 Total Office Disposals in FY2019. Trend interpretation: fewer disposals relative to filings may reflect more first-action approvals for publication and fewer abandonments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average First-Action Pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time between filing of a trademark application and the substantive review that typically results in either a Notice of Publication or a first Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office target range supported by TPAC is 2.5 to 3.5 months; FY2019 result was 2.6 months after a six-month pendency initiative. Used to balance customer needs with incoming filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Total Pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time between filing of a trademark application and final disposition (registration, abandonment, or issuance of a Notice of Allowance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported both excluding and including suspended/inter partes cases: FY2019 = 9.3 months (excluding suspended/inter partes) and 10.7 months (including). Compared against Office targets to evaluate end-to-end processing timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Filing and Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal to have all trademark applications and other filings submitted electronically and to increase end-to-end electronic processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics: >99.9% of new applications submitted electronically; 88.4% of applications processed end-to-end electronically (exceeding target of 88%). Policy change: final rule mandating electronic filing and email designation (implementation planned Dec 21, 2019). Benefits: cost-effective processing, reduced errors, and elimination of paper filing subsidies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance Rate (Examination Quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of actions or decisions determined to have been made correctly (no deficiencies or errors) measured at two points: initial Office Actions and final disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office FY2019 goals: 95.5% compliance for First Office Action and 97% for final compliance. FY2019 results: 96.4% (First Office Action) and 97.4% (final). Evaluation is based on random sample reviews and whether written Office Actions comport with bases of refusal under the Lanham Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional Office Action Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office Action meets the Exceptional standard if it satisfies four criteria: appropriateness of the likelihood of confusion search, quality of the evidence provided, clarity of the writing, and quality of the decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office FY2019 goal: 46% of Office Actions meet the standard; FY2019 result: 54.5%. Used as a qualitative measure of excellence in individual Office Actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and Onboarding Standards for Examining Attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and initiatives to train new Examining Attorneys and standardize onboarding across training law offices and traditional/virtual offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019: 83 new Examining Attorneys hired; Training Unit pilot implemented to standardize on-boarding, classroom training, mentoring, and hands-on learning; TORCH mandatory in-person training event; Nice Classification 11th Edition training; focused sessions on U.S. Counsel rule, digitally created/altered/mockup specimens, and mandatory electronic filing. Emphasis on leadership development for mentors and managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination Guides Usage and Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination Guides provide specific guidance on examination issues, supersede TMEP inconsistencies, and are typically incorporated into the next TMEP edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples issued in FY2019: guidance on cannabis/cannabis-derived goods after the 2018 Farm Bill; Section 2(a) scandalousness after Iancu v. Brunetti; guidance on digitally created/altered/mockup specimens; guidance on implementing the U.S. Counsel rule. Examination Guides clarify procedures where TMEP lacks specific or updated direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: ID Manual Standards for Identifications
rubrics_metrics.description: ID Manual lists identifications of goods/services and classifications Examining Attorneys will accept without further inquiry if specimens support the identification and classification; serves as a guide for what constitutes a sufficiently 'definite' identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not exhaustive; updated for Nice Classification 11th Edition effective 01/01/2019. Enhancements include search/navigation improvements. Used to increase consistency in accepted identifications and support applicants in drafting definite identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Counsel Requirement (Rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule (effective Aug 3, 2019) requiring applicants, registrants, or parties to proceedings whose domicile or principal place of business is outside the U.S. to be represented by an attorney who is an active member in good standing of the bar of the highest court of a U.S. state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: deter unauthorized representation, ensure proper signatures/averments/use claims, and enable enforcement of statutory/regulatory requirements. TPAC supported and commended issuance; Examination Guides provided implementation clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Electronic Filing Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule amending Rules of Practice to mandate electronic filing of trademark applications and associated submissions and to require designation of an email address for USPTO correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published July 31, 2019; implementation planned Dec 21, 2019. Intended to achieve end-to-end electronic processing, improve administrative efficiency, optimize workflow, reduce processing errors, and end subsidization of paper filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random Audits of Proof-of-Use Declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Program to conduct random audits of 'proof of use' declarations under 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.161(h) and 7.37(h) to improve integrity of the Trademark Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019: audits of >5,000 post-registration maintenance affidavits; in 62% of audited registrations either goods/services were deleted or the entire registration was canceled. Audit outcomes tracked by representation status (78% represented by counsel vs 22% pro se).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Specimen Analysis / Specimen Database
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement and use of a commercial off-the-shelf tool to permit automated integrated analysis of trademark specimens to detect fraudulent specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool will use metadata, error analysis, compression, filtering and other methodologies to compare specimens; integrated into Trademark workflow; beta testing expected late 2019. Purpose is proactive detection of fraudulent specimen submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraudulent Solicitation Countermeasures
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts to detect, warn about, and prosecute companies fraudulently promising trademark protection; coordination domestically and via TM5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include public notices, a 'Solicitation Alert' video, two USPTO lawyers detailed to DOJ for prosecution, and a TM5 project creating a multinational database of questionable solicitations and public awareness resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP Security Enhancements
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures to address malicious/damaging inputs to USPTO systems and to protect critical record elements (e.g., correspondence email changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploring requirements for usernames/passwords/PINs and making changes to critical record fields more difficult; interim step: sending emails to trademark owners/applicants when a change of correspondence address is received. Response to increase in fraudulent/unauthorized changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB Performance and Process Initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics and process reforms for the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board, including efforts to declutter the Register, revisions to the TTAB Manual of Procedure, Standard Protective Order review, staffing, performance measures, and precedential decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019 experienced increases in incoming appeals/oppositions/cancellations and cases ready for decision; TTAB could not meet some pendency/inventory goals but met target for number of precedential decisions and increased Accelerated Case Resolution (ACR) cases. Pilot programs encourage early adoption of expedited procedures for abandonment/non-use cancellations; SPO revisions limited to minor clarifying edits based on stakeholder feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee Collection and Budgeting Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee forecasting, fee adjustment capability, and monitoring fee revenues and spending for Trademark Operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019 trademark fees increased 4.5% (within 1% of planned collections). TPAC notes budgeting success depends on ability to adjust fees to reflect filing trends and practices. Discussions included proposed fee adjustments, Financial Advisory Board input, and direct vs indirect spending considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MyUSPTO Service Enhancements
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancements to the MyUSPTO personalized homepage and associated widgets to improve user experience and access to trademark tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2019 additions: Trademark 'Form Finder' widget, mobile trademark application status app with push notifications. Planned: TEAS Plus Short Form filing widget in beta. These features aim to facilitate filing and portfolio management for users.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT Stabilization and Modernization (TMNG focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO focus to stabilize legacy trademark systems and modernize via the Trademark Next Generation (TMNG) effort and OCIO initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns over delays and costs to replace legacy systems; Path Forward Team convened; industry consultant engaged for IT vision/strategy; new approach agreed to deliver a suite of IT products with multi-year execution beginning Q2 FY2020. Emphasis on reducing risk of aging systems and controlling development costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: TM5 International Harmonization Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative international projects among TM5 partners to harmonize trademark tools/practices (ID List, Common Status Descriptors, TMview, bad faith filings, image search, quality management, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: TM5 ID List of harmonized identifications (19,932 terms as of Sept 10, 2019); Common Status Descriptors implemented in TSDR; joint bad faith seminars and reports; collaborative work on non-traditional marks, image search, and quality management. Purpose: improve registrant experience internationally and harmonize practices across major offices.
